Hi Maya / team,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciate the candor on usage patterns. I wanted to capture the bits we agreed to confirm and a few asks so we can model a precise unit-econ proposal. Short recap below.

Call recap (quick):
- Primary use case: automated clinical triage summary + smart intake forms (3 features we demoed).
- Expected traffic: a mix of 1) heavy async batches (nightly digest) and 2) low-latency interactive sessions (clinician assist) — ~70/30 split.
- Volume guidance: you indicated season 1 pilot ~5–12M tokens/month, scaling to 40–120M tokens/month if retention/engagement ramps.
- Procurement timing: internal procurement review in mid-May; final PO expected by end of June if pricing aligns.

Asks / action items (what I owe you and what we need from you):
1) Can you confirm a likely monthly budget band for pilot (ballpark is okay) — you mentioned a $6k–$18k monthly target but we want to be explicit about whether that is TCO for platform + infra or only product line items.
2) For our unit-econ modeling: what is the desired payback window for CAC on this feature set? (you flagged 6–12 months as ideal; please confirm).
3) Any constraints on margin targets? e.g., gross margin target >60% on the feature line, or a fixed CPx target.
4) If you have representative example sessions (a few transcripts or average token counts per session), please drop them into the attached workbook. That will let us produce $/feature estimates rather than just $/1M tokens.

Preliminary numbers from Redwood (for discussion only):
- Inference cost (our estimate): $12–$38 per 1M tokens depending on model/quant and batching policy (we'll tighten after you share session shapes).
- Target customer-facing price bands we typically model for similar customers: $350–$1,200 per 1M tokens, depending on SLAs and feature richness.
- Converted to $/feature (rough): if an average assisted triage flow is 2.5k tokens, the $/feature ranges above map to ~$0.90–$3.00 per triage event (broad).

Notes on CAC / payback:
- If you look for 6-month CAC payback and want >60% gross margin on the feature, that constrains price per feature and therefore the acceptable token price. We'll run scenarios for you once we lock the token shape and the pilot budget.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Ben will follow up with a 2-slide pricing + 3 scenario unit-econ sheet (pilot / scale / aggressive).
- We'll incorporate any example sessions you provide into the Wellbridge_token-estimates.xlsx (attached).
- Proposed quick sync mid-week to land on a binding pilot budget so procurement can be looped in.

Thanks — looking forward to tightening these numbers.

Best,

Maya — great, thanks for confirming the pilot budget target. I pushed a quick model into the workbook (tab: scenario-1). Key things I added and questions for you: 

1) Model assumptions (quick):
   - Baseline inference cost used: $20 per 1M tokens (midpoint of our estimate).
   - Average triage flow: 2,400 tokens (we used a conservative number; will update when you send session exports).
   - Acquisition & integration CAC assumed: $38k one-time for pilot (sales-led + SE time), spread over 9 months = $4.2k/mo amortized.

2) Outcome (pilot band $6k–$12k/mo):
   - $6k/mo pilot (low): at $20/1M tokens we see a negative margin on feature unless price per 1M tokens > $420 (equivalently >= $1.01 per triage).
   - $12k/mo pilot (target): at $20/1M tokens we can hit ~55–60% gross margin if customer price per 1M tokens is in the $480–$820 range (maps to $1.15–$2.00 per triage).

3) CAC payback sensitivity:
   - With an amortized CAC of $4.2k/mo, a $12k pilot yields ~3–5 month payback on the pilot slice alone if conversion/expansion assumptions hold; but across broader clinical conversion the overall product CAC payback ~9 months is achievable under the $480/1M token scenario.

Questions for procurement and product:
- Is the amortized CAC approach acceptable (we included SE hours + onboarding in the one-time bucket)?
- Will you accept a staggered pricing step (pilot discounted month 1–3, then list price) or does procurement want a fixed per-unit price for 12 months?

I attached my scenario notes in the workbook. Happy to walk through at Wednesday 10am PT.

Thanks,
